tier: ISP Proxies (static residential), pay per address, Starter plan floor

free_tier.stated: One-time USD 5.00 Welcome Credit on registration, spent at each product's rates: 'Every new account receives a one-time $5.00 Welcome Credit on registration, added to your balance immediately – no commitment required to start testing products.' It applies per team, not per user, stays valid while the account is on the free plan, and unused credit carries into the first upgrade to a paid plan.
free_tier.notes: The ISP pricing page states 'We offer free credits for ISP Proxies' and 'our ISP Proxies free trial is for a single use'; ISP addresses are priced from USD 1.5/IP ('$1.5/IP Up to 3 IPs').

retention.stated: not applicable: an address, not an object
retention.notes: No stored bytes are involved. Sessions carry no time limit: 'You can keep an IP for as long as you need without worrying about session time.'

egress.terms: Not billed by the byte: 'Unlimited bandwidth with fair usage', explained as 'No additional charges on traffic expenditure with the Pay-per-IP pricing model'; addresses are priced from '$1.5/IP' down to '$1.1/IP' at 2.27K+ IPs. the provider limits concurrency, not bytes: until 50 GB of usage per ISP proxy in a month, 100 concurrent sessions per purchased proxy; once 50 GB is reached, 10 concurrent sessions per proxy for the rest of the billing cycle.

interface_detail: A proxy endpoint, not a REST resource. The quick start lists 'ISP isp.oxylabs.io 8000 user- 8001 and up' and 'Dedicated ISP disp.oxylabs.io 8000 user- 8001 and up' (endpoint, rotating port, username prefix, static ports); the protocol is set by the connection prefix in the proxy client, 'http://', 'https://' or 'socks5h://'. A static address is chosen by port ('use 8001 for IP #1, 8002 for IP #2, etc.'); shared ISP targets a country with '-country-US' in the username, dedicated ISP by the port of an address in that country. Proxy users and instances are set up in the Oxylabs Dashboard. No interface token names a proxy protocol, so 'rest' is the nearest.
endpoint: isp.oxylabs.io:8000 (ISP), disp.oxylabs.io:8000 (Dedicated ISP), static ports 8001 and up
tooling: Any client that takes an HTTP, HTTPS or SOCKS5 proxy. The product page links integration guides for Puppeteer, Selenium, Playwright, Scrapy, AdsPower, GoLogin, Multilogin and Octo Browser, and an Agent Skills repository (github.com/oxylabs/agent-skills) of SKILL.md files for AI agents.
chaining: The outbound address layer of an HTTP client: bytes are not billed ('No additional charges on traffic expenditure with the Pay-per-IP pricing model'), so cost follows the address count, from USD 1.5/IP with the smallest plan Starter at USD 30/mo, and the limit that applies is which targets the ISP network carries; restricted targets open only 'after you go through a short KYC procedure'.

limits.value: target blocklist rather than a rate: 'Some websites are restricted on our ISP Proxy network'; the list 'includes but is not limited to' entertainment and streaming (Netflix, Spotify, Twitch, Disney), banking and other financial institutions (PayPal, Bank of America, Binance), government websites (usa.gov, canada.ca), gaming (Playstation, Steam), ticketing (Ticketmaster, Eventbrite) and mailing (Outlook, Yahoo mail)
semi-dedicated, not exclusive: the product page labels the addresses 'Semi-dedicated IPs' and the pricing page lists 'Shared with up to 3 users'

fair usage limits concurrency: until 50 GB of usage per ISP proxy in a month, 100 concurrent sessions per purchased proxy; once 50 GB is reached, 10 concurrent sessions per proxy for the rest of the billing cycle, applied automatically, with an email notice at 80% and at 100% of the data allowance
none: 'Unlimited bandwidth', explained as 'No additional charges on traffic expenditure with the Pay-per-IP pricing model'

limits_note: Two constraints have no limit kind. The plan floor is a minimum spend: the smallest self-service plan is Starter at USD 30/mo. The target blocklist refuses destinations rather than rating requests ('We restrict some websites for ISP Proxies'); it is filed under request-rate as the nearest kind, and listed targets can be opened 'after you go through a short KYC procedure'.
binding_note: The target blocklist binds ('We restrict some websites for ISP Proxies'): bytes are not billed ('Unlimited bandwidth with fair usage'), and the provider limits concurrency rather than volume, at 100 concurrent sessions per purchased proxy until 50 GB of usage per proxy in a month and 10 per proxy after that for the rest of the billing cycle.

identity_cost.detail: Paid plans take 'Credit card payments', PayPal, Google Pay, Apple Pay, or wire transfers through the sales or account-manager teams; 'Please note that we do not accept cryptocurrency payments.' What registration asks for, and whether the welcome credit needs a payment method, is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: Addresses are 'hosted on a data center but registered under ISPs' and 'Shared with up to 3 users'. Past 50 GB of usage per proxy in a month, concurrency drops from 100 to 10 sessions per proxy for the rest of the billing cycle. Listed targets are refused unless opened 'after you go through a short KYC procedure'. Self-service purchases are non-refundable.
confidence_note: Documented: the per-IP ladder, the plan floor, the welcome credit, the protocol list, the fair-usage concurrency limits and the restricted-target notice are on the vendor's ISP pricing page. No address has been bought, so no request through an ISP address and no answer from a restricted target is measured.

evidence.proved: The per-address ladder - 'ISP Proxies $1.5/IP Up to 3 IPs', '$1.5/IP Up to 20 IPs', '$1.4/IP Up to 71 IPs', '$1.2/IP Up to 416 IPs', '$1.1/IP 2.27K+ IPs' - plus the plan floor 'Starter $30/mo', 'Welcome credits FREE $5 toward any product', and 'Unlimited bandwidth with fair usage'.
The decisive sentence for the registration class: 'Static Residential Proxies originate from datacenter proxies, therefore they are just as fast as their counterparts.'

The product's own words: 'Semi-dedicated IPs', 'Unlimited-duration sessions', 'HTTP, HTTPS, and SOCKS5 protocols', 'UDP and TCP connection', the bullet 'Unlimited bandwidth' with its explanation 'No additional charges on traffic expenditure with the Pay-per-IP pricing model', and the premium ASN names Lumen, Comcast, BT Group, Orange and Cox Communications.

The target blocklist, and where it lives: 'Some websites are restricted on our Residential Proxy network to avoid abuse and unclear activities', then 'The list includes but is not limited to targets such as:' 'All Apple domains', 'Some Google domains', 'Government websites'. The sentence is not on any of the three ISP pages - all three were fetched and grepped for 'restricted on our' and returned zero matches - so the blocklist is attributed to this page and not to the ISP product pages.

How the address is reached: 'ISP isp.oxylabs.io 8000 user- 8001 and up' and 'Dedicated ISP disp.oxylabs.io 8000 user- 8001 and up', with the protocol chosen by connection prefix - 'http://, https://, or socks5h://' - and a static port per address, '8001 for IP #1, 8002 for IP #2, etc.'

notes: The vendor states the class two ways on its static residential page: 'Static Residential Proxies originate from datacenter proxies, therefore they are just as fast as their counterparts', and they are 'datacenter IPs assigned via a contract with an Internet Service Provider (ISP)' that 'receive their IPs from internet service providers, such as British Telecom, Comcast'. No per-address ASN or hosting-provider list is published, so the ASN that announces an issued address is unverified: behind a purchase. The page states a pool of over 100K static residential IPs and lists 'Shared with up to 3 users' without saying whether that counts dashboard users or buyers of one address. The same page says 'there are no limits or restrictions to any of your targets', while the ISP network's restricted-target list is in limits.
